premise: A passenger jet runs out of fuel at cruising altitude and the pilots glide it to a landing on a disused airfield.
known_facts: Air Canada Flight 143 was a Boeing 767 flying from Montreal to Edmonton in July 1983.
69 people were aboard: 61 passengers and 8 crew.
Both engines failed at about 41,000 feet because the aircraft had been fuelled with the wrong amount of fuel.
The airline's fleet was in the middle of switching from pounds to kilograms, and the crew's fuel calculation mixed up the units.
The captain was an experienced glider pilot.
The aircraft glided to Gimli, Manitoba, a former air force base then used for car racing.
The nose gear collapsed on landing, but nobody was killed.
Racers and spectators were on the former runway when the aircraft landed.
